interpretations.low: Start by checking facts and looking for the root cause of deviations.
interpretations.medium: You analyse work situations. Strengthen the habit of testing assumptions.
interpretations.high: You spot inconsistencies and find their causes. Apply this skill when reviewing complex cases.

interpretations.low: Practise stating your position calmly and asking for help.
interpretations.medium: You're ready to take responsibility. Practise discussing decisions with solid arguments.
interpretations.high: You state your position confidently and take responsibility. Help colleagues speak up about risks.

interpretations.low: Build steady routines for starting and finishing your shift.
interpretations.medium: You follow the core rules. Make recording results a daily habit.
interpretations.high: You follow processes consistently. Share a checklist that works with your team.

interpretations.low: Start by understanding how your work contributes to the overall result on site.
interpretations.medium: You take part in team life. Try suggesting an improvement to a related process.
interpretations.high: You see the bigger picture and support colleagues. Try yourself as a mentor.

questions.1: The shift starts soon. How will you check readiness, and what will you do if a permit or PPE is missing?
questions.2: The drawing differs from actual site conditions. What will you check before deciding whether work can start?
questions.3: An experienced colleague breaks a technical rule. What will you say, and what if they disagree?
questions.4: A neighbouring crew is behind schedule. How will you help while accounting for your own tasks?
questions.5: You are asked to skip a checklist item to save time. How will you respond and explain your decision?
questions.6: An experienced colleague gives an instruction that seems questionable. How will you verify it and agree on next steps?
questions.7: How does your work affect the next construction stages? Give an example and explain how you account for it.
questions.8: An urgent decision is needed and your manager is unavailable. How will you define your authority and act?
questions.9: The shift has ended, but quantities and issues are not recorded. What will you do now and next time?
questions.10: You notice a problem outside your area of responsibility. What will you do to get it resolved?
questions.11: Defects or delays recur on your site. How will you find the root cause and check that a fix worked?
questions.12: You doubt a conclusion before handing over work. What evidence will you use, and when will you request a review?
questions.13: You are pushed to change the technical sequence. How will you assess the situation and respond?
questions.14: A newcomer asks you to share a work technique. How will you explain it and check they can use it safely?
questions.15: Reinforcement does not match the design. The crew says: “We always do it this way.” Describe and explain your actions in order.
